---
title: "Question 3: My First Interactive Dashboard"
format: dashboard
server: shiny
---

```{r}
#| context: setup
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)

# Turn R's built-in Titanic summary table into one row per passenger
titanic <- as.data.frame(Titanic) |>
  uncount(Freq)
```

## {.sidebar}

### Choose a group

```{r}
selectInput("sex", "Passenger group", choices = c("All", "Male", "Female"), selected = "All")
```

This first example uses R's built-in Titanic data. Choose a group, then explore survival counts.

## Survival

### Row {height=65%}

```{r}
plotlyOutput("survival_plot")
```

### Row {height=35%}

```{r}
DTOutput("passenger_table")
```

## Passenger details

### Row {height=100%}

```{r}
DTOutput("details_table")
```

```{r}
#| context: server
selected_titanic <- reactive({
  if (input$sex == "All") titanic else filter(titanic, Sex == input$sex)
})
output$survival_plot <- renderPlotly({
  p <- selected_titanic() |>
    count(Class, Survived) |>
    ggplot(aes(Class, n, fill = Survived, text = paste("Passengers:", n))) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    labs(x = "Passenger class", y = "Number of passengers", fill = "Survived") +
    theme_minimal()
  ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
})
output$passenger_table <- renderDT({ datatable(selected_titanic() |> count(Sex, Class, Survived), options = list(pageLength = 5)) })
output$details_table <- renderDT({ datatable(selected_titanic(), options = list(pageLength = 10)) })
```
